exposure: Type of cesarean section (emergency vs. non-emergency)
outcome: Surgical site infection (SSI) after cesarean section
cohort: The study included 384 women who underwent cesarean sections at Imam Khomeini Hospital in Ahvaz.
finding: Surgical site infections after cesarean sections were significantly associated with factors such as maternal education, body mass index, number of previous surgeries, premature rupture of membranes, emergency cesarean sections, gestational diabetes, length of hospitalization, singleton births, and maternal employment.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections were associated with higher surgical site infection rates compared to non-emergency procedures.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively for cases between April 1, 2021, and April 30, 2022.
